title: Chulalongkorn University and Qunova Computing Execute MoU to Advance Hybrid Quantum Algorithms for Industrial R&D - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Thailand's Chulalongkorn University signed a three-year MoU with South Korean quantum software developer Qunova Computing to deploy hybrid quantum-classical algorithms — including Qunova's high-accuracy VQE variants developed with KAIST — against chemistry, fluid dynamics and financial modelling problems. The deal sits inside Thailand's explicit 'cloud-first' strategy of renting international QPU backends instead of fabricating domestic hardware, and adds Qunova to a Siam Quantum Square roster that already includes AIST, IBM Thailand, Western Digital and SCB X.

insights.claim: Thailand has an explicit national cloud-first quantum strategy that prioritizes cloud-based access to international QPU backends over domestic hardware fabrication, a deliberate decision to skip the capital-intensive hardware layer.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Countries choosing rent-not-build create recurring demand for quantum cloud access; the monetizable layer is software and compute hours, not fabs.
insights.quote: which prioritizes cloud-based access to international QPU backends over domestic hardware fabrication
insights.locator: The alliance aligns with Thailand’s national “cloud-first” quantum computing strategy

insights.claim: Chulalongkorn University signed a three-year MoU with South Korean quantum software developer Qunova Computing covering joint R&D, researcher exchanges and applied deployment of hybrid quantum-classical algorithms.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A three-year term is shorter than the parallel AIST deal, suggesting a narrower, application-specific engagement; no funding figure is disclosed.
insights.quote: Thailand’s Chulalongkorn University has signed a three-year Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with South Korean quantum software developer Qunova Computing.

insights.claim: Qunova Computing and KAIST are deploying specialized hybrid algorithms including Qunova's high-accuracy Variational Quantum Eigensolver variants, anchoring the collaboration in NISQ-era error-mitigated methods rather than fault-tolerant assumptions.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Betting on VQE-class methods means near-term deliverables but also exposure to the well-documented scaling limits of variational algorithms.
insights.quote: including Qunova’s high-accuracy Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE) variants
insights.locator: Under the MoU, Qunova Computing and the Korea Advanced Institute

insights.claim: Target workloads are named at the problem level rather than the technology level — molecular simulation for pharmaceutical lead optimization, computational fluid dynamics for industrial manufacturing, and portfolio optimization across regional bond markets.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Regional bond portfolio optimization is an unusual, concrete quantum use case worth tracking; most such announcements stop at generic chemistry.
insights.quote: molecular simulation for pharmaceutical lead optimization, computational fluid dynamics for industrial manufacturing, and portfolio optimization across regional bond markets
insights.locator: The joint focus groups target specific domain applications

insights.claim: Domain problems are being sourced from named Thai institutions — Faculty of Medicine Siriraj Hospital for clinical and pharmaceutical work and SCBX Public Company Limited for financial optimization — giving the algorithms real industrial data rather than benchmark instances.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Access to proprietary clinical and banking datasets is the scarce input in applied quantum; this is more differentiating than the algorithms themselves.
insights.locator: [ Chulalongkorn University & Qunova Computing Strategic Framework ]

insights.claim: Siam Quantum Square is accumulating a multi-vendor roster — AIST (G-QuAT), IBM Thailand, Western Digital, SCB X and now Qunova — making Chulalongkorn a neutral aggregation point that plays hardware and software providers against each other.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Vendor-neutral national hubs erode any single quantum provider's lock-in in emerging markets; expect thin margins on these access deals.
insights.quote: complementing its existing institutional collaborations with AIST (G-QuAT), IBM Thailand, Western Digital, and SCB X.
insights.locator: The partnership expands Siam Quantum Square’s international ecosystem

insights.claim: Two separate quantum MoUs — one with Japan's AIST and one with South Korea's Qunova — were executed through the same Chulalongkorn hub, indicating Thailand is deliberately multi-sourcing its quantum dependencies across North Asian partners.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Multi-sourcing across Japan and Korea is a hedge against single-country technology dependence; the competitive win goes to whoever converts an MoU to paid deployment first.
insights.locator: The partnership expands Siam Quantum Square’s international ecosystem
